name: Emirati Air Quality Index (UAE)

sources.title: National Center of Meteorology, Guideline for calculating the Emirati Air Quality Index (EAQI), 2023, Table 3

categories.label: Moderate
categories.health: Acceptable for the majority of the population.

categories.label: Unhealthy
categories.health: A greater proportion of the public may be affected.

categories.label: Hazardous
categories.health: The entire population is expected to be affected.

rules: US-EPA (2018) method: SI = (I_hi - I_lo)/(BP_hi - BP_lo) x (C - BP_lo) + I_lo, using truncated concentrations. O3, SO2, NO2, PM10 are truncated to 1 ug; CO to 0.1 mg; PM2.5 to 0.1 ug.
Each sub-index is rounded half-up to an integer. EAQI = max sub-index.
O3: compute both the 1-h and 8-h sub-indices and take the larger. A 1-h value below the national standard (200 ug) is not used. When the 8-h value exceeds 392, only 1-h is used.
SO2: when the 1-h value exceeds 797, the 24-h rolling mean is used.
Rolling means need at least 6 of 8 or 18 of 24 valid hours. With fewer: the sub-index is null if all hours are below the national standard, otherwise the maximum hourly value is used.
Hourly values above the validation thresholds (CO 150.4 mg; SO2 1750.4; NO2 2000.4; O3 1000.4; PM 2500.0 ug) are treated as invalid.
notes: Two cases the guideline does not specify, decided by us: (1) above the top breakpoint but below the validation threshold (e.g. PM10 600-2500), we extrapolate along the top band and flag beyond_scale. (2) 1-h SO2 > 797 while the 24-h mean is < 798: sub-index = 200, following the US-EPA 2018 Technical Assistance Document that the guideline builds on.
Table 2 and Table 3 of the guideline differ slightly (e.g. CO 'Good' is 0-5 in Table 2 and 0.0-5.4 in Table 3). The guideline says to compute with Table 3, so we do.
The worked O3 example mentions breakpoints '125 and 169' but computes with 121/167. Our test asserts the published result: 135.485 ug gives 116.
